owner: W-68, after his word
file: components/shell/CourseSidebar.module.css .rail (a transition on width); components/shell/NavSearch.module.css @keyframes nav-search-grow (width)
what: NEEDS HIS WORD (the side panel's mechanics are out of scope, and the search field's slide is a look he approved on 2026-09-30; decision 3). The only two motions the app has today both animate width, which lays the page out again on every frame, and they are the two motions he meets most. They are the two exceptions to this pass's rule that what moves, moves by transform and opacity. The lead's remedy, if "minimal motion" is to hold everywhere: under 1024px the drawer slides in by transform over --motion-enter-lg and its scrim fades; from 1024px up the side panel switches with no motion; the search field fades in and moves 8px, and Sync steps aside at once. Default taken: both stay as they are, and only their times and curves read the new tokens (the entry time-tokens-shell, which is in the default build).

what: FOR THE PM TO RULE (a test binds; decision 6). One scrollbar keeps its arrow buttons after the build: the Upcoming strip, the block he named. Its pinned rule (scrollbar-width: thin with scrollbar-color) makes Chromium draw the standard thin bar with two arrows and a grey track, and its own three ::-webkit-scrollbar rules are dead for the same reason. To make it the app's bar: drop scrollbar-width and scrollbar-color from .tracker, so those three rules come alive (they can keep the visible track R3-1 asks for), and change the two assertions of the test. Default until he rules: leave it. The tile says under the strip that this one bar is the old kind.
